H2.title: Summary state cue drifts from the ingest fragment it claims to share
H2.resolution: ROUND 2 - the behaviour is closed, not just the claim. Round 1 corrected the false 'the cue cannot drift from the fragment by construction' comment and deliberately kept the page-load snapshot; a cue that lies is a defect whether or not the comment admits it, and the owner's decision on re-review was to fix it properly. _ingest_status_fragment now appends a TOP-LEVEL <code id="ingest-state-cue" hx-swap-oob="true"> carrying that branch's OWN literal status token, so every response that re-renders the body also re-renders the cue: the 2s poll (H2's direction - `running` over a settled success body), the terminal 286 that stops the poll, and the 202 returned when a run is started in-page (M2's sharper direction - `success`/`none` over a live run). The cue is NOT a second read of the row: it is the fragment's own token, so there is one reader and nothing left to disagree with. Guarded by TestSummaryCueIsRefreshedOutOfBand in tests/test_ui_m12_corpus_before_machinery.py - every branch parametrised, plus a top-level-position guard, because a NESTED hx-swap-oob is inert and would fail exactly like the original bug.

H3.title: Collapsing the disclosure hides the ingest error path with no recovery
H3.resolution: Closed by the OOB state cue, which is the primary remedy this finding itself proposed ('make the cue live instead of a snapshot, zero new JS'). The <summary> is rendered even when the disclosure is shut, so _ingest_status_fragment's top-level <code id=ingest-state-cue hx-swap-oob=true> now changes 'running' -> 'success'/'failed' under a collapsed operator on every poll branch, including the terminal 286. MITIGATED, NOT DISSOLVED, and the difference is recorded: stderr_tail still lives inside the collapsed subtree, so the operator sees THAT the run failed without expanding but must expand to read WHY. The larger alternative (hoist #ingest-status out of the disclosure entirely, brief-2 section 5.3) remains the road not taken.

M9.resolution: Relaxed to a direction-agnostic form. The guard required the empty copy to contain the literal 'Manage this notebook' - i.e. to BE a pointer to a form elsewhere on the page - which is exactly what ui-uplift-m11 AC#1 forbids, and m11 depends_on m12 and owns empty-state copy. m12 had pinned its declared successor out of satisfying its own first AC. Kept the durable half (the copy must not point 'above', the FACT m12 corrected and m11 cannot legitimately reverse); dropped the direction, which is m11's to choose.

M12.title: Region 3 is absent from heading navigation and has no accessible name
M12.resolution: The <details> now carries aria-labelledby resolving to its own <summary>'s id. HTML-AAM maps <details> to role=group, so region 3 is announced by name on entry - previously it contributed NOTHING to the heading list (the summary is a role=button, whose children are presentational, so nesting an <h2> was correctly refused and nothing replaced it), and the heading list silently gained or lost five entries with the open state. Zero structural cost, no change to m8's ^<(section|div)> record view. Mutation-verified.

L2.title: `list-style-position: outside` is unexplained and its m10 justification does not transfer
L2.resolution: The reason is recorded. list-style-position: outside was the one declaration in this milestone's rule set with no rationale; it was copied from .discover-abstract > summary, where it is REQUIRED because that rule sets overflow:hidden + max-height and an inside marker would be clipped. This rule sets neither, so it is visual parity only - it aligns the label's text edge with the sibling h2s and the marker hangs into body's 1rem (main has no padding). Kept rather than dropped, because dropping it misaligns the label against every other region heading. test_the_summary_needs_no_marker_clipping_workaround pins that this rule declares no overflow/max-height, so nobody re-derives the m10 requirement for it.

L9.resolution: The record now states the condition.
